sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. Pair with sender_device_id for cross-signing binding.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

device_proof.description: Optional per-device transport proof block. Schema-open extension point keyed by device-lifecycle.md §5.2 cross-signing binding (typical sub-fields: cross_signing_binding, sender_device_key_fingerprint, signature_over_content_digest). MUST NOT replace MLS authentication of the enclosing envelope; included only when an additional out-of-band per-device transport binding is required (e.g. SAS verification, dehydrated-device proofs). Receivers MUST treat unknown sub-fields as opaque and MUST NOT trust device_proof in isolation.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

secret_request_content.description: ck.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. SHOULD be the device hpke_key or the ephemeral key already established by the bound SAS verification transcript.

secret_send_content.description: ck.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ck.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at_unix} where request_id/secret_id are the outer ck.secret.send content fields and expires_at_unix is expires_at normalized to integer Unix seconds (device-lifecycle.md §10.7); both sides reconstruct it from the DeviceMessageEnvelope plus content. Freshness for sent_at (server-assigned) is bound by the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.

realm_key_request_content.description: ck.realm_key.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §13.2). A read-eligible receiver asks a concrete key source to evaluate policy and, if authorized, deliver historical history_secret material via durable ck.realm_key.share or an equivalent policy-authorized recovery path. Carries no key material itself.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: Recipient device HPKE public key (KeyPackage init key or equivalent) the key source MUST verify as an authorized device key for recipient_principal_id before sealing history_secret.

requested_source_class.description: Source class this request targets. key_backup is intentionally excluded because it is retrieved via ck.self.keys.backups.command.unlock.

target_source_ref.description: Concrete source this request is routed to: a device_id for own_device / verified_member_device, or a service DID for archive_node / recovery_service. Service-targeted reuse of this to-device kind is valid only when ServiceDescribe exposes a concrete recipient_device_id / queue target for the service DID; otherwise the service MUST expose a dedicated operation.

target_principal_id.description: Principal that owns target_source_ref (the to-device queue is addressed by (principal, device_id)). Carried so the relay routes directly without scanning Realm members to reverse-lookup the device's principal.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the requested key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}.

policy_digest.description: Optional requester-observed policy digest hint. The key source MUST recompute the effective policy from accepted history before sharing.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional requester-observed membership frontier hint. The key source MUST recompute recipient eligibility from accepted history before sharing.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

pairing_code.description: Short user-visible code bound into a same-principal device authorization transcript.

new_device_pubkey.description: Public key material for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. The kid SHOULD equal the requesting device id and the object is later consumed by ck.gate.account.command.pair_device.

challenge_signature.description: Fresh requesting-device proof bound to pairing_code, new_device_pubkey, gate_audience, and request_canonical_digest; later submitted to ck.gate.account.command.pair_device.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.
